q:
Which of the following statements is correct with reference to Preventive Maintenance of assets?
1. It enhances the availability of the assets.
2. It enhances the reliability of the assets.

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 2 only: preventive maintenance, carried out at planned intervals before failure occurs, is aimed at keeping the asset dependable in service, i.e. it enhances the reliability of the asset.

q: The balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense (WMS) represents:

options.A: The value of finished stock held in stores depots
options.B: The value of labour, material and on-cost booked on jobs in progress in the workshop
options.C: The arrears of pay of workshop staff
options.D: The book value of machinery and plant in the workshop

e: The WMS balance represents work-in-progress: the labour, material and on-cost booked on jobs still under execution in the workshop and not yet transferred out on completion.

q: In workshop accounts, on-cost is generally distributed over jobs on the basis of:

options.A: Cost of material consumed
options.B: Direct labour charges
options.C: Machine hours only
options.D: Floor area of the shop

e: On-cost is absorbed on jobs generally as a percentage of direct labour charges, since indirect workshop expenses vary broadly with the labour employed on jobs.

q: Which of the following items forms part of 'proforma on-cost' in a workshop?

options.A: Wages of direct shop staff
options.B: Provident Fund contribution and depreciation of workshop plant and buildings
options.C: Cost of raw material issued to jobs
options.D: Power consumed by shop machines

e: Proforma on-cost consists of notional charges such as Provident Fund contribution and depreciation of workshop plant and buildings, debited so that the true cost of outturn is reflected.

q: In workshop accounts, the abbreviation WGR stands for:

options.A: Workshop Gate Register
options.B: Workshop General Register
options.C: Wages Grant Register
options.D: Weekly Goods Return

e: WGR stands for Workshop General Register, the register in which work orders, the expenditure booked on them and the outturn transferred are recorded job-wise.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Rolling Stock Programme (RSP) covers procurement of locomotives, coaches and wagons.
2. The Machinery and Plant (M&P) Programme covers workshop machinery and plant.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the Rolling Stock Programme covers procurement of locomotives, coaches and wagons, while the Machinery and Plant Programme covers workshop machinery and plant.

q: The difference between the time/tally sheets and the labour pay sheets in a workshop is ordinarily charged to:

options.A: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.B: Shop on-cost
options.C: General on-cost
options.D: Proforma on-cost

e: The difference between the time/tally sheets and the labour pay sheets cannot be allocated to specific jobs, so it is charged to shop on-cost.

q: Revenue Standing Work Orders in a workshop are characterised by the fact that they:

options.A: Are issued afresh for every single job
options.B: Remain unchanged from year to year for routine revenue jobs
options.C: Cannot be used for repair work
options.D: Are sanctioned by the Railway Board every year

e: Revenue Standing Work Orders bear fixed numbers that remain unchanged from year to year and are used for routine, repetitive revenue jobs of the shop.

q: The authority on the basis of which manufacture is undertaken in a railway workshop is the:

options.A: Route card
options.B: Gate pass
options.C: Stock sheet
options.D: Advice of Internal Check

e: Manufacture in a workshop is undertaken on the authority of the route card, which prescribes the operations to be performed and the sequence in which the job moves.

q: Under the Group Incentive Scheme in railway workshops, the incentive is linked to:

options.A: Individual output of each worker
options.B: The outturn of the group/shop as a whole
options.C: The number of days present
options.D: The savings in material cost only

e: Under the Group Incentive Scheme, bonus depends on the outturn of the group or shop as a whole, not on the output of an individual worker.

q: In workshop costing, 'on-cost' refers to:

options.A: The wages of workers directly engaged on a job
options.B: The cost of material issued to a job
options.C: Indirect expenses which cannot be directly identified with or allocated to a particular job
options.D: The profit added to the cost of a job

e: On-cost means indirect expenses which cannot be directly identified with or allocated to a particular job and are therefore absorbed over jobs on a suitable basis.

q: Shop on-cost comprises:

options.A: The indirect expenses incurred within a particular shop
options.B: The expenses common to the workshop as a whole
options.C: Charges debited notionally, such as depreciation
options.D: The direct wages paid in the shop

e: Shop on-cost comprises the indirect expenses incurred within a particular shop, as distinct from general on-cost, which is common to the workshop as a whole.

q: General on-cost comprises:

options.A: The cost of raw material for all shops
options.B: The bonus paid under the incentive scheme
options.C: The direct labour charges of the workshop
options.D: Indirect expenses common to the workshop as a whole, such as general administration and supervision

e: General on-cost comprises indirect expenses common to the workshop as a whole, such as general administration and supervision, apportioned among the shops.

q: Proforma on-cost in workshop accounts consists of charges which are:

options.A: Paid in cash by the workshop every month
options.B: Debited notionally, such as Provident Fund contribution and depreciation, so that the true cost of outturn is reflected
options.C: Recovered from the staff as fines
options.D: Booked only on jobs done for other railways

e: Proforma on-cost consists of charges debited notionally, such as Provident Fund contribution and depreciation, so that the cost of outturn reflects its true cost.

q: In the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense (WMS) Budget, the head 'Issues to Stores' represents:

options.A: Stores purchased directly from the market
options.B: Material returned by shops to the depot
options.C: Material manufactured in the workshop for stocking in stores depots
options.D: Scrap sold through auction

e: 'Issues to Stores' in the WMS budget represents articles manufactured in the workshop for stocking in stores depots, transferred out of WMS on completion.

q: On completion of a job, the amount accumulated under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is cleared by transfer to:

options.A: The Station Earnings account
options.B: Stores, Revenue or Capital heads, as applicable to the job
options.C: The Pension Fund
options.D: The Contingency Fund

e: On completion of a job, the amount accumulated under WMS is cleared by transfer to Stores, Revenue or Capital heads, as applicable to that job.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. WMS balances tend to increase when jobs remain incomplete and open for long periods.
2. WMS balances can be kept low by prompt completion of jobs and prompt transfer of the outturn to Stores or the respective demands.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: balances grow while jobs remain incomplete and open, and they are kept low by prompt completion of jobs and prompt transfer of outturn.

q: Part II of the Workshop Outturn Statement shows:

options.A: The quantity of outturn of each shop
options.B: The outlay, i.e. the expenditure incurred on the jobs
options.C: The list of machines in the shop
options.D: The arrears of wages of shop staff

e: Part II of the Workshop Outturn Statement shows the outlay, i.e. the expenditure incurred on the jobs, while Part I shows the outturn of each shop.

q: Under the CLW pattern incentive scheme followed in railway workshops, the bonus of a worker is linked to:

options.A: The total outturn of the entire workshop
options.B: His individual performance, i.e. the time saved by him on a job against the allowed time
options.C: The number of years of service put in
options.D: The savings in the cost of material

e: Under the CLW pattern, a worker's bonus is linked to his individual performance, measured by the time saved by him on a job against the allowed time.

q: The cost of material used in the Periodic Overhaul (POH) of home railway rolling stock in a workshop is booked under:

options.A: PU 11
options.B: PU 27
options.C: PU 32
options.D: PU 35

e: The cost of material used in the Periodic Overhaul of home railway rolling stock in a workshop is booked under PU 35.

q: Under job costing in a workshop:

options.A: The cost of all jobs is pooled together at the end of the year
options.B: Expenditure on labour, material and on-cost is accumulated separately for each job under its work order
options.C: Only material cost is recorded job-wise
options.D: Costs are recorded shop-wise but never job-wise

e: Under job costing, expenditure on labour, material and on-cost is accumulated separately for each job under its own work order, so that the cost of each job is known.

q: In a railway workshop, the time books and gate attendance cards primarily serve as the record of:

options.A: Attendance and time of arrival and departure of workshop staff
options.B: Material issued to jobs
options.C: Machines under repair
options.D: Visitors entering the workshop

e: Time books and gate attendance cards primarily record the attendance of workshop staff, i.e. their time of arrival and departure.

q: The time spent by a workshop employee on individual jobs is recorded through:

options.A: Stock sheets
options.B: Route cards only
options.C: Job cards
options.D: Completion reports

e: The time spent by an employee on individual jobs is recorded through job cards, which show the job-wise distribution of his time.

q: Production workshops of Indian Railways are distinguished from repair workshops in that production workshops:

options.A: Carry out only periodic overhaul of coaches
options.B: Manufacture new rolling stock such as locomotives, coaches and wagons
options.C: Do not maintain any accounts
options.D: Are located only in Railway Board's office complex

e: Production workshops manufacture new rolling stock such as locomotives, coaches and wagons, whereas repair workshops carry out overhaul and repairs of existing stock.

q: Itemised proposals for inclusion in the Rolling Stock Programme (RSP) are submitted by the zonal railways to:

options.A: The C&AG of India
options.B: The Ministry of Finance
options.C: The Railway Board
options.D: The respective State Governments

e: Itemised proposals for inclusion in the Rolling Stock Programme are submitted by the zonal railways to the Railway Board.

q: In railway workshops, WAMS stands for:

options.A: Workshop Accounts Management System
options.B: Workshop Asset Monitoring Service
options.C: Wages and Allowance Management Scheme
options.D: Workshop Administration and Maintenance Schedule

e: WAMS stands for Workshop Accounts Management System, the computerised system used for workshop accounts work.

q: A process shop in a workshop is one in which:

options.A: Only one single job is undertaken at a time
options.B: Production flows continuously through standardised processes
options.C: No incentive scheme is in operation
options.D: All work is done manually without machines

e: A process shop is one in which production flows continuously through standardised processes, unlike a job shop handling varied specific orders.

q: The accounts office of a workshop compiles and renders, for its transactions, a periodical:

options.A: Station Balance Sheet
options.B: Advice of Internal Check
options.C: Account Current
options.D: Traffic Book

e: The accounts office of a workshop compiles and renders an Account Current for its transactions, linking them with the general books of the railway.

q: Material issued from stores for execution of a workshop job is initially debited to:

options.A: The final Revenue head of the job
options.B: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense, under the respective work order
options.C: The Stock Adjustment Account
options.D: The shop on-cost account directly

e: Material issued from stores for a workshop job is initially debited to Workshop Manufacturing Suspense under the respective work order, pending completion of the job.

q: Wages paid to workshop staff for idle time, which cannot be charged to any job, are charged to:

options.A: A specific work order chosen by the shop incharge
options.B: The Pension Fund
options.C: The Capital head of the workshop
options.D: Shop on-cost

e: Wages paid for idle time, which cannot be charged to any job, are charged to shop on-cost.

q: In workshop accounts, the Workshop General Register (WGR) is maintained primarily to record:

options.A: The attendance of workshop staff
options.B: The price ledger of stores items
options.C: The muster roll of casual labour
options.D: Job-wise details of work orders in progress, the expenditure booked on them and the outturn transferred

e: The Workshop General Register records job-wise details of work orders in progress, the expenditure booked on them and the outturn transferred out of WMS.

q: The total cost of jobs in progress as per the Workshop General Register should agree with:

options.A: The balance under Stores Suspense
options.B: The balance under Traffic Suspense
options.C: The balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense in the general books
options.D: The balance of the shop on-cost account

e: The total cost of jobs in progress as per the Workshop General Register should agree with the balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense in the general books.

q: Periodical review of the Workshop General Register by the Workshop Accounts Officer is aimed mainly at:

options.A: Detecting jobs lying incomplete or outstanding for long periods and securing their early clearance
options.B: Fixing the pay of workshop staff
options.C: Preparing the annual budget of the Railway
options.D: Verifying the cash balance of the workshop cash office

e: Periodical review of the WGR by the Workshop Accounts Officer detects jobs lying incomplete or outstanding for long periods so that their early clearance is secured.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Expenditure under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense can be incurred only against a work order issued for the job.
2. A work order is issued on the basis of a sanctioned estimate or an authorised programme/indent.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: WMS expenditure can be incurred only against a work order, and a work order is issued on a sanctioned estimate or an authorised programme/indent.

q: Articles manufactured in a railway workshop are taken into stores stock at:

options.A: Cost of manufacture, i.e., material, labour and on-cost
options.B: The prevailing market price
options.C: Direct material cost only
options.D: A fixed rate notified by the Railway Board for all workshops

e: Articles manufactured in a workshop are taken into stores stock at their cost of manufacture, i.e. material, labour and on-cost booked on the job.

q: Scrap and released material arising from a workshop job is:

options.A: Credited to the job (work order) at its assessed value
options.B: Debited additionally to the job as extra material cost
options.C: Credited to the Pension Fund
options.D: Sold directly by the shop incharge

e: Scrap and released material arising from a job is credited to the job (work order) at its assessed value, thereby reducing the net cost of the job.

q: Material drawn for a job but found surplus and returned to the stores depot is accounted for by:

options.A: Debiting Workshop Manufacturing Suspense once again
options.B: Writing off its value to shop on-cost
options.C: Treating it as scrap sale
options.D: Crediting its value to the work order from which it was drawn

e: Material drawn for a job but returned surplus to the stores depot is accounted for by crediting its value to the work order from which it was drawn.

q: Jobs executed by a workshop for the use of its own Railway are transferred:

options.A: At market rates with an element of profit
options.B: At cost, without any profit element
options.C: At rates fixed by the C&AG
options.D: At 10 per cent above cost

e: Jobs executed for the use of the workshop's own railway are transferred at cost, without any profit element.

q: On-cost is charged to workshop jobs at rates which are:

options.A: Decided by each shop incharge month to month
options.B: Always equal to 100 per cent of the material cost
options.C: Predetermined on the basis of anticipated indirect expenses and anticipated direct labour
options.D: Notified in the Stores Code

e: On-cost is charged to jobs at predetermined rates fixed on the basis of anticipated indirect expenses and anticipated direct labour for the period.

q: The general on-cost of a workshop is apportioned among the shops generally on the basis of:

options.A: Floor area occupied by each shop
options.B: Number of machines installed in each shop
options.C: Direct labour charges of each shop
options.D: Number of staff in each shop

e: The general on-cost of a workshop is apportioned among the shops generally on the basis of the direct labour charges of each shop.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Proforma on-cost is charged so that the cost of workshop outturn becomes comparable with market/trade rates.
2. Proforma on-cost represents an actual cash outgo of the workshop.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 only: proforma on-cost is charged so that workshop outturn cost becomes comparable with market/trade rates; it is a notional charge, not an actual cash outgo, so statement 2 is wrong.

q: Wages of direct workers for periods of authorised leave, which cannot be booked to any particular job, are charged to:

options.A: A capital work order
options.B: The next job undertaken by the worker
options.C: Stores Suspense
options.D: Shop on-cost

e: Wages of direct workers for periods of authorised leave cannot be booked to any particular job and are therefore charged to shop on-cost.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Overtime wages paid for a specific urgent job are charged to that job.
2. Overtime wages not attributable to any specific job are charged to on-cost.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: overtime wages for a specific urgent job are charged to that job, while overtime not attributable to any specific job is charged to on-cost.

q: Ordinary repairs and maintenance of a shop's own machinery and plant are charged to:

options.A: The Capital head of the workshop
options.B: Shop on-cost
options.C: The job running on the machine at that time
options.D: Stores Suspense

e: Ordinary repairs and maintenance of a shop's own machinery and plant are charged to shop on-cost, being an indirect expense of that shop.

q: The estimates of on-cost charges of a workshop form part of:

options.A: The Traffic Book
options.B: The Stores Budget only
options.C: The Works Programme of the Railway
options.D: The workshop budget, prepared along with the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense estimates

e: The estimates of on-cost charges form part of the workshop budget, which is prepared along with the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense estimates.

q: Bonus earned by workers under the incentive scheme in a workshop is accounted for as:

options.A: Part of the labour cost, charged to the respective jobs/work orders
options.B: A charge to the Staff Benefit Fund
options.C: General on-cost in all cases
options.D: A deduction from the material cost of jobs

e: Bonus earned under the incentive scheme is part of the labour cost of the jobs and is charged to the respective jobs/work orders on which it was earned.

q: A specific (shop) work order differs from a standing work order in that it is:

options.A: Valid for all routine work of the shop for the whole year
options.B: Issued only by the Railway Board
options.C: Issued for a particular identified job, whereas a standing work order covers routine repetitive work
options.D: Never closed even after completion of work

e: A specific (shop) work order is issued for a particular identified job, whereas a standing work order covers routine, repetitive work of a class.

q: Standard components manufactured in lots for stocking in stores depots are executed under:

options.A: Batch work orders, with the cost accumulated for the batch as a whole
options.B: Revenue standing work orders only
options.C: Verbal instructions of the shop incharge
options.D: Material requisitions alone

e: Standard components manufactured in lots for stocking in stores depots are executed under batch work orders, with the cost accumulated for the batch as a whole.

q: Every work order issued in a workshop must invariably indicate:

options.A: The name of the worker who will execute the job
options.B: The head of account/allocation to which the cost of the job is chargeable
options.C: The market price of the finished article
options.D: The date of the next POH of the workshop

e: Every work order must invariably indicate the head of account/allocation to which the cost of the job is chargeable, so that expenditure is booked correctly.

q: Once a workshop job is completed and its work order is closed:

options.A: Further charges may be booked to it till the end of the year
options.B: Only material can be booked to it thereafter
options.C: Only labour can be booked to it thereafter
options.D: No further expenditure can be booked to that work order

e: Once a job is completed and its work order closed, no further expenditure can be booked to that work order.

q: Material issued from stores to a workshop job is priced at:

options.A: The latest market rate on the date of issue
options.B: The rate at which the material was manufactured
options.C: A rate fixed by the shop incharge
options.D: The stores price-ledger (issue) rate

e: Material issued from stores to a workshop job is priced at the stores price-ledger (issue) rate, not at the market rate of the day.

q: Part I of the Workshop Outturn Statement shows:

options.A: The outlay incurred on the jobs of each shop
options.B: The outturn, i.e., the work done/completed by each shop
options.C: The on-cost percentages of the workshop
options.D: The balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense

e: Part I of the Workshop Outturn Statement shows the outturn, i.e. the work done/completed by each shop, while Part II shows the outlay incurred.

q: On completion of a workshop job, a completion report is prepared in order to:

options.A: Record the final cost of the job and compare it with the sanctioned estimate
options.B: Fix the pay of the staff who worked on the job
options.C: Close the workshop accounts for the month
options.D: Revise the stores price ledger

e: On completion of a job, a completion report is prepared to record the final cost of the job and compare it with the sanctioned estimate.

q: The labour pay sheets of a workshop are prepared by:

options.A: The shop incharge from the route cards
options.B: The Personnel Branch from the leave records
options.C: The Accounts office from the time/tally sheets rendered by the shops
options.D: The Cash office from the attendance register

e: The labour pay sheets are prepared by the Accounts office from the time/tally sheets rendered by the shops.

q: In the internal check of workshop labour pay sheets, the Accounts office ensures, among other things, that:

options.A: The time booked to jobs agrees with the job cards/tally sheets
options.B: All workers are paid only in cash
options.C: The outturn of the shop exceeds the programme
options.D: Material issues are within the Average Annual Consumption

e: In the internal check of labour pay sheets, the Accounts office ensures that the time booked to jobs agrees with the job cards/tally sheets.

q: The 'CLW pattern' of incentive scheme in railway workshops takes its name from:

options.A: Central Labour Workshop
options.B: Chittaranjan Locomotive Works
options.C: Carriage and Locomotive Workshop, Perambur
options.D: Central Locomotive Works, Varanasi

e: The CLW pattern of incentive scheme takes its name from Chittaranjan Locomotive Works, where this pattern of individual incentive based on time saved was evolved.

q: Under the incentive scheme, the 'allowed time' for a job is fixed on the basis of:

options.A: Negotiation with the recognised union
options.B: The shop incharge's rough estimate
options.C: The actual time taken on the job in the previous year
options.D: Time studies (work measurement) carried out by the rate fixer

e: The allowed time for a job under the incentive scheme is fixed on the basis of time studies (work measurement) carried out by the rate fixer.

q: The Group Incentive Scheme is mainly in vogue in:

options.A: Production units manufacturing new locomotives
options.B: Repair workshops carrying out POH and repairs of rolling stock
options.C: Stores depots
options.D: Railway printing presses only

e: The Group Incentive Scheme is mainly in vogue in repair workshops carrying out POH and repairs of rolling stock, where outturn is a group effort.

q: Under the Group Incentive Scheme, incentive is computed on the basis of:

options.A: Only such outturn as is passed and accepted
options.B: All outturn including rejected work
options.C: Attendance of the group members alone
options.D: Savings in material cost alone

e: Under the Group Incentive Scheme, incentive is computed only on such outturn as is passed and accepted; rejected work earns no incentive.

q: Under the individual incentive scheme, 'time saved' by a worker means:

options.A: Time taken minus the allowed time
options.B: Hours of attendance minus idle time
options.C: Allowed time minus the actual time taken by him on the job
options.D: Allowed time minus the leave availed by him

e: Time saved by a worker means the allowed time for the job minus the actual time taken by him on it.

q: Which of the following is NOT covered under the Rolling Stock Programme (RSP)?

options.A: Procurement of new locomotives
options.B: Procurement of new coaches
options.C: Procurement of new wagons
options.D: Periodic overhaul of existing rolling stock, which is a revenue activity

e: Periodic overhaul of existing rolling stock is a revenue activity and is not covered under the Rolling Stock Programme, which provides for procurement of new stock.

q: The cost of new machinery and plant for a workshop is provided through:

options.A: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.B: The Machinery and Plant (M&P) Programme, charged to Capital/DRF as applicable
options.C: Shop on-cost
options.D: Revenue standing work orders

e: The cost of new machinery and plant for a workshop is provided through the Machinery and Plant (M&P) Programme, charged to Capital/DRF as applicable.

q: In workshops, the cost of Periodic Overhaul is compiled and compared in terms of:

options.A: Cost per worker employed
options.B: Cost per square metre of shop area
options.C: Cost per unit (per coach/wagon/locomotive) overhauled
options.D: Cost per stores requisition

e: The cost of Periodic Overhaul is compiled and compared in terms of cost per unit (per coach/wagon/locomotive) overhauled.

q: The annual programme of a repair workshop lays down, among other things:

options.A: The pay scales of workshop staff
options.B: The stores purchase plan of the Railway
options.C: The list of machines to be condemned
options.D: The number of units (coaches/wagons) programmed for periodic overhaul during the year

e: The annual programme of a repair workshop lays down, among other things, the number of units (coaches/wagons) programmed for periodic overhaul during the year.

q: The total cost of a Periodic Overhaul job in a workshop comprises:

options.A: Labour, material and on-cost booked under the POH work orders
options.B: Material cost only
options.C: Labour cost only
options.D: Material cost and departmental charges only

e: The total cost of a Periodic Overhaul job comprises labour, material and on-cost booked under the POH work orders.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The cost of additional (new) machinery under the M&P Programme is charged to Capital.
2. The cost of replacement of existing machinery under the M&P Programme is charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: additional (new) machinery under the M&P Programme is charged to Capital, while replacement of existing machinery is charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund.

q: Job costing, as followed in railway workshops, is also known as:

options.A: Process costing
options.B: Specific order costing
options.C: Operation costing
options.D: Marginal costing

e: Job costing is also known as specific order costing, because costs are collected for each specific job or order undertaken.

q: A 'job shop' in a workshop is a shop which:

options.A: Undertakes a variety of jobs, each executed to a specific order/requirement
options.B: Runs one continuous standardised process throughout the year
options.C: Only stocks finished goods manufactured elsewhere
options.D: Does no repair work at all

e: A job shop undertakes a variety of jobs, each executed to a specific order or requirement, unlike a process shop running a continuous standardised process.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The cost of special tools and jigs consumed on a particular job is charged to that job.
2. The cost of small tools of general use in a shop is charged to shop on-cost.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: special tools and jigs consumed on a particular job are charged to that job, while small tools of general use are charged to shop on-cost.

q: Material is drawn from the stores depot for a workshop job against:

options.A: A verbal demand of the worker
options.B: An authorised requisition (issue note) quoting the work order
options.C: The route card alone, without any requisition
options.D: The completion report of the previous job

e: Material is drawn from the stores depot for a job against an authorised requisition (issue note) quoting the work order to which it is chargeable.

q: The Workshop Manufacturing Suspense budget estimates of a workshop are framed on the basis of:

options.A: The cash balance of the workshop at the end of the previous year
options.B: The anticipated programme of manufacture and repair work (outturn) for the year
options.C: The number of staff due to retire during the year
options.D: The stores purchases made in the previous year

e: The WMS budget estimates are framed on the basis of the anticipated programme of manufacture and repair work (outturn) planned for the year.

q: Expenditure booked under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense on jobs remaining incomplete at the close of the financial year represents:

options.A: A loss to be written off during the year
options.B: Revenue earnings of the workshop
options.C: Work-in-progress, carried forward under WMS to the next year
options.D: Dead surplus stock of the workshop

e: Expenditure on jobs remaining incomplete at the close of the financial year represents work-in-progress, carried forward under WMS to the next year.

q: The full cost of an article manufactured in a workshop is arrived at by adding proforma on-cost to:

options.A: Direct labour cost alone
options.B: Direct material cost alone
options.C: The selling price of the article
options.D: The prime cost plus shop on-cost and general on-cost

e: The full cost of a manufactured article is the prime cost plus shop on-cost and general on-cost, with proforma on-cost added to it.

q: Rolling stock is taken up for Periodic Overhaul in a workshop:

options.A: Whenever a minor defect is noticed in service
options.B: On completion of the prescribed periodicity (arisings) of the stock
options.C: Only after it meets with an accident
options.D: At the discretion of the station master of the home station

e: Rolling stock is taken up for Periodic Overhaul on completion of its prescribed periodicity, i.e. as arisings of stock become due for overhaul.

q: The Workshop Accounts Office of a railway workshop is headed by:

options.A: The Controller of Stores
options.B: The Travelling Inspector of Accounts
options.C: The Principal Chief Engineer
options.D: The Workshop Accounts Officer

e: The Workshop Accounts Office of a railway workshop is headed by the Workshop Accounts Officer.

q: In a workshop cost sheet, the 'works cost' (shop cost) of a job comprises:

options.A: Prime cost plus general on-cost and proforma on-cost
options.B: Direct material cost only
options.C: Prime cost plus proforma on-cost only
options.D: Prime cost plus shop on-cost

e: In a cost sheet, the works cost (shop cost) of a job comprises prime cost plus shop on-cost; general and proforma on-cost are added thereafter for full cost.

q: The cost per article of a batch-manufactured item is arrived at by:

options.A: Dividing the direct labour cost of the batch by the number of articles
options.B: Dividing the total cost of the batch by the number of work orders issued
options.C: Dividing the total cost of the batch by the number of articles produced in the batch
options.D: Adopting the market price of a similar article

e: Cost per article of a batch item = total cost of the batch divided by the number of articles produced in the batch.

q: A cost sheet for a manufactured job in a workshop is compiled:

options.A: On completion of the job, from the costs accumulated under its work order
options.B: Before the work order is issued, as a rough forecast only
options.C: At the close of the year, for all jobs together in one sheet
options.D: By the stores depot when the article is taken into stock

e: A cost sheet for a manufactured job is compiled on completion of the job, from the labour, material and on-cost accumulated under its work order.

q: The shop on-cost percentage applied to jobs is worked out as:

options.A: Total shop on-cost divided by total material cost of the shop
options.B: Total direct labour divided by total shop on-cost
options.C: Total shop on-cost divided by the number of jobs done in the shop
options.D: Total shop on-cost divided by total direct labour charges of the shop, expressed as a percentage

e: Shop on-cost percentage = total shop on-cost divided by total direct labour charges of the shop, expressed as a percentage.

q: The prime cost of a workshop job consists of:

options.A: Direct material and shop on-cost only
options.B: Direct labour and general on-cost only
options.C: Direct material, direct labour and direct expenses chargeable to the job
options.D: All costs of the job including proforma on-cost

e: The prime cost of a job consists of direct material, direct labour and direct expenses chargeable to that job.

q: Hire charges of special equipment engaged exclusively for a particular job are treated as:

options.A: Shop on-cost of the shop
options.B: A direct expense charged to that job as part of its prime cost
options.C: General on-cost of the workshop
options.D: A proforma charge on the job

e: Hire charges of special equipment engaged exclusively for a particular job are a direct expense of that job and form part of its prime cost.

q: Where on-cost is absorbed on jobs at predetermined rates, the difference between the on-cost so absorbed and the actual on-cost incurred is known as:

options.A: Work-in-progress
options.B: Suspense balance
options.C: Departmental charges
options.D: Over-absorption or under-absorption of on-cost

e: Where on-cost is absorbed at predetermined rates, the difference between the on-cost absorbed and the actual on-cost incurred is the over-absorption or under-absorption of on-cost.

q: Idle time of workshop staff is recorded primarily through:

options.A: Completion reports
options.B: Route cards
options.C: Material requisitions
options.D: Idle time cards/statements showing the period and reasons for idleness, certified by the shop supervision

e: Idle time is recorded through idle time cards/statements showing the period and reasons for idleness, certified by the shop supervision.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The time booked by a worker on job cards plus his recorded idle time should account for his total attendance time as per the gate/time cards.
2. Unaccounted differences between attendance time and booked time are investigated by the Accounts office.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: a worker's time on job cards plus his recorded idle time should equal his attendance time, and unaccounted differences are investigated by the Accounts office.

q: For a period of recorded idle time caused by circumstances beyond his control (e.g., power failure), a worker under the incentive scheme:

options.A: Earns bonus at the average rate of the shop for that period
options.B: Is paid wages at the time rate for the idle period, but earns no bonus on that period
options.C: Is paid no wages for the idle period
options.D: Has the idle period treated as leave without pay

e: For idle time caused by circumstances beyond his control, such as power failure, the worker is paid wages at the time rate but earns no bonus for that period.

q: Under the Halsey premium bonus plan, the bonus payable to a worker is generally:

options.A: 50 per cent of the value of the time saved by him
options.B: 100 per cent of the value of the time saved by him
options.C: 25 per cent of his total time wages
options.D: Equal to his total time wages for the job

e: Under the Halsey plan, bonus = 50 per cent of the value of the time saved, i.e. 50 per cent of (time saved x hourly rate).

q: Under the Rowan premium bonus plan, the bonus earned by a worker is calculated as:

options.A: 50 per cent of the value of time saved
options.B: Time saved multiplied by the hourly rate
options.C: Time taken multiplied by the hourly rate
options.D: (Time saved / Time allowed) x Time taken x hourly rate

e: Under the Rowan plan, bonus = (time saved / time allowed) x time taken x hourly rate, so the bonus proportion rises with efficiency but by a diminishing share.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Halsey plan, the worker receives a fixed percentage (commonly 50 per cent) of the value of time saved, whatever the level of saving.
2. Under the Rowan plan, the bonus is a fixed percentage of the worker's time wages at every level of time saved.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 only: under Halsey the worker gets a fixed percentage (50 per cent) of the value of time saved; under Rowan the bonus is not a fixed percentage of time wages, so statement 2 is wrong.

q: In work measurement for the incentive scheme, the 'allowed time' for a job is the:

options.A: Time actually taken by the fastest worker in the shop
options.B: Normal time for the job plus the prescribed allowances (e.g., fatigue/relaxation allowance)
options.C: Time taken on the same job in the previous year
options.D: Time fixed by negotiation with the staff side

e: The allowed time for a job is the normal time for the job plus the prescribed allowances, such as fatigue/relaxation allowance, determined by work measurement.

q: Bonus under the incentive scheme is payable only on:

options.A: All jobs done in the workshop, whether measured or not
options.B: Jobs done by indirect workers of the shop
options.C: Measured jobs for which allowed times have been fixed
options.D: Jobs done on standing work orders only

e: Bonus under the incentive scheme is payable only on measured jobs for which allowed times have been fixed through work study.

q: A worker under the incentive scheme who fails to save any time on a job is:

options.A: Paid only half of his time wages
options.B: Paid no wages for that job
options.C: Charged with the value of the time lost
options.D: Still guaranteed and paid his full time-rate wages for the time worked

e: A worker who saves no time on a job is still guaranteed and paid his full time-rate wages for the time worked; only the bonus is not earned.

q: The efficiency of a worker under the incentive scheme, expressed as a percentage, is generally worked out as:

options.A: (Allowed time / Actual time taken) x 100
options.B: (Actual time taken / Allowed time) x 100
options.C: (Time saved / Actual time taken) x 100
options.D: (Time wages / Bonus earned) x 100

e: Efficiency of a worker = (allowed time / actual time taken) x 100; efficiency above 100 per cent indicates time saved on the job.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The total labour cost distributed to jobs from the tally/time sheets must agree with the total wages as per the labour pay sheets, after providing for items chargeable to on-cost.
2. This agreement is a basic internal check exercised in the workshop accounts office.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: labour distributed to jobs from tally sheets must agree with the labour pay sheets after providing for on-cost items, and this agreement is a basic internal check.

q: The tally (time) sheets rendered by a shop show, worker-wise:

options.A: Only the total attendance of the shop for the day
options.B: The distribution of each worker's time over the jobs on which he was engaged during the period
options.C: The wages payable to each worker for the month
options.D: The bonus earned by the shop as a whole

e: Tally (time) sheets show, worker-wise, the distribution of each worker's time over the jobs on which he was engaged during the period.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Material specifically requisitioned and consumed on a particular job is charged to that job.
2. Consumable stores of general use in a shop (e.g., cotton waste, lubricating oil for general use) are charged to shop on-cost and not to individual jobs.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: material specifically requisitioned for a job is charged to that job, while consumable stores of general use are charged to shop on-cost.

q: Material purchased specifically for a particular job and not taken into depot stock is:

options.A: Charged to Stores Suspense and held there till the job is completed
options.B: Charged to shop on-cost of the shop
options.C: First taken into stock and then issued to the job
options.D: Charged directly to the work order of that job

e: Material purchased specifically for a particular job, and not taken into depot stock, is charged directly to the work order of that job.

q: Standing work orders in a workshop are characterised by:

options.A: A fresh number allotted for every occasion of use
options.B: Fixed numbers allotted to specified classes of routine/repetitive work, against which charges are booked as and when such work is done
options.C: Numbers allotted by the Railway Board for each item of work
options.D: No number at all, being identified only by the shop name

e: Standing work orders bear fixed numbers allotted to specified classes of routine/repetitive work, against which charges are booked as and when such work is done.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The work order is the authority under which expenditure on a job is booked to the allocation indicated on it.
2. The route card indicates the sequence of operations and the shops through which the job passes.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the work order is the authority for booking expenditure to the allocation shown on it, and the route card shows the sequence of operations and shops.

q: A copy of every work order issued in a workshop is sent to the Workshop Accounts Office mainly so that:

options.A: It can fix the wages of the staff who will work on the job
options.B: Charges booked against the work order can be watched and the job cost compiled in the Workshop General Register
options.C: It can purchase the material required for the job
options.D: It can sell the finished articles of the job

e: A copy of every work order is sent to the Workshop Accounts Office so that charges booked against it can be watched and the job cost compiled in the Workshop General Register.

q: Material drawn for a job and later returned to the stores depot as surplus is credited to the job:

options.A: At the same price at which it was issued to the job
options.B: At the current market price on the date of return
options.C: At half of its issue price
options.D: At a price fixed by the shop incharge

e: Material returned to the stores depot as surplus is credited to the job at the same price at which it was issued to the job.
